annotation_comments.text: First detected in the developing limb at Carnegie stage 14 (CS14), proximal to the progress zone. Between CS15 and CS16, as the mesenchyme condenses to form catilaginous primordial bone, expressed in the middle part of the developing limb, outlining the pre-cartilaginous structure of the bone. The strongest expression is observed in the perichondrium and condensing mesenchyme, but it is also detected in the overlying ectoderm. At CS18 and CS21, remains confined to the middle portion of the arm, around the distal end of the humerus, the radius and ulna, and in some bones of the wrist. No detected in the phalanges, but expressed in the overlying ectoderm of the fingers. A similar pattern of expression is observed in the lower limb. Also expressed in the mesenchymal core of the first and second pharyngeal arches, with expression starting at CS15. Expression increases until CS21 as the mesenchyme condenses.

annotation_comments.text: It is hypothesized that SHOX may contribute to the difference in height between men and women. Although the SHOX gene is located in the pseudoautosomal region PAR1 of the X and Y chromosomes and is assumed to escape chromosome X inactivation, it is thought that SHOX gene expression from inactivated X chromosome is nevertheless lower than that from active X or Y chromosomes. Small, but persistent sex differences in SHOX expression dosage may lead to the variation in the sex steroid-independent childhood growth function, thereby yielding the sex difference in height.

annotation_comments.text: At 6.5 dpc, not detected in the embryo, but present in a few cells of the mother's mesometrium. From 8 dpc onwards, embryonic expression is detected in mesoderm derivatives that contribute to bone and cartilage formation in the limbs, ribs, palate, nasal capsula, prepuce, and spinal cord (PubMed:9466998, PubMed:9482898). Between 12.5 and 15.5 dpc, craniofacial expression is observed in cells condensing around the developing eyelid, nasal cavity, and palate. As the palate fuses and the nasal capsula differentiates, th expression is down-regulated and only remains detectable in the tips of the fusing palate. During the same time interval, expressed in heart and metanephric mesoderms. In the heart, expression is restricted to the developing outflow track and the developing aorta. In the ectoderm, found in the developing brain, spinal, and otic ganglia (PubMed:9482898). In the developing extremities, detected at 9.5 dpc in mesodermal cells on the dorsal side of the limb bud. As the limb bud develops, this expression intensifies in the mesoderm of the progress zone and in undifferentiated mesoderm condensing around the ossification centers. At 12.5 dpc, detected in the mesoderm of the anterior tip of the growing limb and in mesenchymal cells condensing around the cartilage primordium of fore and hind limb bones. At 14.5 dpc, expressed in mesodermal condensations at the periphery of the developing phalanges. At this stage, first detected in differentiating presumptive bone regions. Expression decreases between 14.5 and 16.5 dpc, but is still detectable in ossification centers of long bones as limb skeletal parts chondrify (PubMed:10749976, PubMed:9466998, PubMed:9482898).
